title: Authors' code manifest
description: On-disk record written at retrieval to <attempt_dir>/authors-code-manifest.json (reproduction-executor v1.2; preparation prompt v1.2 section 1.0.2). It records a sha256 for every authors' file as retrieved, the copies the run executed, the reproducer's own files (wrappers), and any declared edit to an authors' file. scripts/reproduction-lane.py check-attempt (gate 1.1) and check-code verify it: an executed copy must be byte-identical to its retrieved original; any difference must be a declared edit, which is flagged for human ruling; an undeclared difference fails the gate. Rulings: Shawn 2026-10-04, fail-and-uplift follow-on (3); queued amendment 3 item 7(d), wrapper boundary cases (mechanics in wrappers only, never in the authors' files). v1.1 (2026-10-05, after the cross-model review of PR #7): each original may carry a provenance anchor, verified against a committed record the executor did not write (an evidence pack's published deposit checksum bound to the registry's AP-12 version, or the corpus manifest's sha256); an original without a verified anchor is flagged. Wrapper role 'generated' declares code the run itself produced. Paths are relative to the attempt directory, except archive paths, which may name the corpus store with the prefix $CORPUS_ROOT/.

no_authors_code_reason.description: Required when originals is empty: why no authors' code exists to hash (for example, the paper releases none). Executed must then be empty.

originals.description: Every authors' file as retrieved, hashed at the moment of retrieval.

id.description: The file's path within the authors' materials (deposit, repository, or supplement), e.g. analysis/paper/paper.qmd. Unique.

sha256.description: sha256 of the bytes as retrieved.

source.description: URL, DOI plus file name, repository plus tag or commit, or corpus-store path the file came from.

version.description: Deposit version, tag, or commit retrieved (the AP-12 version where one is determined).

local_copy.description: Pristine copy kept in the attempt directory, never edited. When present the gate re-hashes it.

archive.description: When the file was extracted from an archive (a Zenodo zip, a supplement zip). The gate re-extracts the member and re-hashes it. The path is relative to the attempt directory, or begins $CORPUS_ROOT/ for an archive held in the corpus store (deposit archives and publisher supplements may not enter git).

derivation.description: When the authors' code exists only in a form that cannot be executed as bytes (for example, listings printed in a PDF) and the original recorded here is a deterministic transcription. The hash then identifies the transcription, not the publisher's file.

anchor.description: Independent provenance for the original's bytes (gate 1.3). kind evidence-pack: record_id (e.g. zenodo:10.5281/zenodo.10782943) and file (the deposit file key whose published checksum the deposit copy must match; the copy is archive.path or local_copy). The gate chooses the pack itself (newest corpus/evidence-packs/harvest-*/<slug>.json holding the record, then corpus/evidence-packs/<slug>.json); an optional pack field must name one of those. kind corpus-manifest: manifest (a registered corpus manifest), entry (this paper's slug), and filename (a file in the corpus store); it verifies only a journal supplement of a paper whose registry holds its principal artefact there. kind git: repository, commit, path, and blob_sha1, checked against the bytes, with the remote left to a reviewer. kind none: reason. Every record an anchor relies on must exist unchanged at the run's launch commit (check-attempt --launch-commit); without a verified anchor the original is flagged.

executed.description: Every authors' file the run executed or read as code, by the path the run used.

original.description: The id of the retrieved original this copy must equal byte for byte.

declared_edit.description: Present only when the executed copy is NOT byte-identical to its original. Declaring the edit turns a gate failure into a flag for human ruling: whether it is routine mechanics placed in the wrong file or a fail-and-uplift edit is not the gate's call.

wrappers.description: Every code file the reproducer wrote (run scripts, Dockerfile, comparison aids, tools). Mechanics belong here, never in the authors' files.

role.description: generated: code the run itself produced (it must be absent from the pre-run snapshot, and no wrapper may load it).

value_identity_check.description: For role conversion: a JSON record {check: value-identity, result: identical, converter: {path, sha256}, input: {path, sha256}, output: {path, sha256}, values_compared, values_total}, naming this wrapper at its current sha256 and the declared conversion input and output, bound to the current files with full scope. Anything else is flagged as missing, unreadable, failed, unbound, stale, or incomplete.

conversion.description: For role conversion: the input the wrapper converts and the output it writes (paths relative to the attempt directory, or $CORPUS_ROOT/...). The value-identity evidence must name exactly these, and this wrapper at its current sha256.
